DescriptionList.usage: Use for detail data; use Table when values should be compared across rows.

fieldProps.label: Field label where supported by the control
fieldProps.helperText: Supporting or corrective text where supported by the control
fieldProps.error: Error state where supported by the control

Form/Field.description: Figma's Form/Field is a mapping pattern, not a new React component. Compose it using the corresponding props exposed by each Form control.

agentGuidance.apiAuthority: Use the installed dist/index.d.ts for the complete React API. The components entries map public components to Figma and record the design-system contract; do not infer missing React props from this mapping.

principles.name: MonoSchemes geometry
principles.rule: Build hierarchy with spacing, typography, and one-pixel divisions. Keep layout corners square and avoid decorative shadows.

principles.name: Semantic color
principles.rule: Use semantic color variables from the package stylesheet. Do not add raw hex/RGB values or local copies of token definitions.

principles.name: Inverse zone
principles.rule: Use data-theme="inverse" for a region that needs the opposite theme from its parent. It adapts to both page themes. Do not nest inverse zones or replace one with a fixed dark region.

Button.intent: Perform an action in the current view.
Button.whenToUse: Use for submit, save, create, confirm, and other actions.
Button.avoidWhen: Use Link or a navigation item when the interaction navigates to another location.
Button.composition: Use one primary action per decision area; use secondary or tertiary actions for supporting actions.
Button.accessibility: Give icon-only buttons a label. Use type="submit" for form submission and retain visible keyboard focus.

Link.intent: Navigate to a resource or location.
Link.whenToUse: Use for inline or standalone navigation.
Link.avoidWhen: Do not use as a substitute for an action button.
Link.composition: Place inline links in explanatory text or use them as secondary navigation.
Link.accessibility: Use a meaningful label and a real href. Keep the built-in focus-visible treatment.

Text.intent: Apply the system's type scale and semantic text colors.
Text.whenToUse: Use for headings, body copy, labels, captions, and a single leading display headline.
Text.avoidWhen: Do not use repeated display styles for ordinary section headings.
Text.composition: Choose the smallest style that establishes the needed hierarchy; use display-1, display-2, or display-3 only for a leading figure or headline. The display alias is deprecated.
Text.accessibility: Use a semantic heading level through the as prop and keep heading order meaningful.

Form/Input.intent: Collect a single line of text, including email, phone, URL, or search text.
Form/Input.whenToUse: Use when the value is a short textual input.
Form/Input.avoidWhen: Use Form/Password, Form/Number, Form/Date, Form/Time, or Form/Textarea for those specialized roles.
Form/Input.composition: Use FormInput with a visible label and helper or error text where needed.
Form/Input.accessibility: Set label, name, and inputType as appropriate; forward required and autoComplete when applicable.

Form/Password.intent: Collect a password with the built-in show/hide control.
Form/Password.whenToUse: Use for password entry and confirmation.
Form/Password.avoidWhen: Do not build a password reveal control around FormInput.
Form/Password.composition: Pair with an adjacent recovery Link and the form's submit Button when appropriate.
Form/Password.accessibility: Provide a visible label, name, autoComplete, and required state; keep the reveal button's accessible label.

Form/Select.intent: Choose one value from a finite list of options.
Form/Select.whenToUse: Use for a single selection such as language or country.
Form/Select.avoidWhen: Use Form/Multi-select for multiple selections or SegmentedControl for a small always-visible choice.
Form/Select.composition: Provide options as value/label pairs and a visible field label.
Form/Select.accessibility: Keep the label visible and provide a clear placeholder or current value.

Form/Checkbox.intent: Choose an independent boolean option or opt in/out.
Form/Checkbox.whenToUse: Use when an option does not exclude other checkboxes.
Form/Checkbox.avoidWhen: Use Form/Radio or SegmentedControl for mutually exclusive choices; use Form/Toggle for an immediate on/off setting.
Form/Checkbox.composition: Group related choices under a visible fieldset label when there is more than one.
Form/Checkbox.accessibility: Associate each checkbox with its label and expose the checked state through the component API.

Form/Toggle.whenToUse: Use for a setting that takes effect immediately or is clearly a boolean preference.
Form/Toggle.avoidWhen: Use Checkbox for form consent or a choice that is submitted with other fields.
Form/Toggle.composition: Place the label beside the control and group related preferences vertically.
Form/Toggle.accessibility: Keep a persistent label and expose the current boolean state; do not indicate state using color alone.

Tabs.intent: Switch between related panels within the same view.
Tabs.whenToUse: Use for a small set of peer sections that share the same context.
Tabs.avoidWhen: Use navigation for distinct routes or SegmentedControl for an immediate value choice without content panels.
Tabs.composition: Pair each Tab value with a TabPanel using the same value.
Tabs.accessibility: Set aria-label on the tab list and preserve the built-in arrow-key, Home, and End navigation.

SegmentedControl.intent: Choose one option from a small, visible set.
SegmentedControl.whenToUse: Use for immediate choices such as Light/Dark or a compact view mode.
SegmentedControl.avoidWhen: Use Tabs when each choice switches a content panel; use FormSelect for longer option lists.
SegmentedControl.composition: Provide stable values and short labels; store the selected value in the parent.
SegmentedControl.accessibility: Provide aria-label and keep the radio-group arrow-key behavior.

AppHeader.intent: Provide the app's global identity, primary navigation, and actions.
AppHeader.whenToUse: Use at the top of an application shell.
AppHeader.avoidWhen: Do not add a second mobile menu or duplicate navigation that AppHeader already renders.
AppHeader.composition: Pass nav and actions explicitly; use SideNav for section navigation within the application.
AppHeader.accessibility: Use concise labels for icon actions and ensure the mobile menu controls its navigation panel.

SideNav.intent: Navigate between sections of one application area.
SideNav.whenToUse: Use for persistent, hierarchical or category navigation beside the main content.
SideNav.avoidWhen: Use AppHeader/Nav for global destinations or Tabs for switching panels in one view.
SideNav.composition: Render SideNavItem children and mark the current destination selected.
SideNav.accessibility: Keep the nav heading meaningful and provide a real href for navigation items when possible.

Stat.intent: Present one concise metric with its label and optional unit.
Stat.whenToUse: Use for key figures in a dashboard or summary.
Stat.avoidWhen: Do not use as a substitute for a full chart or dense data table.
Stat.composition: Group related Stat components in a responsive layout; add Card only when the content needs a container.
Stat.accessibility: Keep the label understandable when read together with the value and unit.

Table.intent: Present records with shared columns and row relationships.
Table.whenToUse: Use when users need to compare or scan multiple structured records.
Table.avoidWhen: Use cards or a list for independent, unaligned content; do not place an entire application inside a table cell.
Table.composition: Define columns and rows; cells may contain React nodes such as Tag for a status.
Table.accessibility: Use descriptive column headings and keep row actions operable and labelled.

Pagination.intent: Move through a large, paged result set.
Pagination.whenToUse: Use below a table or list when results are split across pages.
Pagination.avoidWhen: Omit it when the full result set is small enough to show at once.
Pagination.composition: Calculate pageCount from the filtered result set and reset the page when filters change.
Pagination.accessibility: Keep the component's navigation label and current-page semantics.

EmptyState.intent: Explain why a section has no content and offer a useful next step.
EmptyState.whenToUse: Use for no results, first-use, or unavailable content states.
EmptyState.avoidWhen: Do not show it alongside stale results or use it for a transient loading state; use Skeleton while loading.
EmptyState.composition: State the condition plainly and provide a recovery action when one exists.
EmptyState.accessibility: Use a clear title and concise description; make action controls keyboard accessible.
EmptyState.example: <EmptyState title="No results" description="Change or clear your filters." actions={<Button label="Clear filters" />} />

DescriptionList.intent: Present a small set of term/value details for one record.
DescriptionList.whenToUse: Use on detail pages for metadata and key/value facts.
DescriptionList.avoidWhen: Use Table when the same fields must be compared across multiple records.
DescriptionList.composition: Pass each label as term and its value as description; descriptions can contain links or Tags.

Form/Field.intent: Describe the shared label, helper text, and error pattern around a form control.
Form/Field.whenToUse: Map the Figma field wrapper to the label, helperText, and error props supported by the chosen Form control.
Form/Field.avoidWhen: Do not create a separate React FormField wrapper unless a future API decision adds one.
Form/Field.composition: Form/Field is a Figma-only mapping to existing Form controls, not an exported React component.

Card/Feature.intent: Summarize one feature with an icon, title, and short description.
Card/Feature.whenToUse: Use for a small set of peer benefits or capabilities.
Card/Feature.avoidWhen: Use Card for arbitrary content; avoid using feature cards for dense records better represented by Table.
Card/Feature.composition: Place a repeated set in a responsive grid and keep descriptions concise.
Card/Feature.accessibility: Keep a meaningful title and do not rely on the icon alone to convey the feature.
Card/Feature.example: <FeatureCard icon="palette" title="Shared tokens" description="One semantic system across themes." />

Footer.intent: Provide closing site identity, navigation, and legal information.
Footer.whenToUse: Use Footer default for a full site footer or Footer minimal for a compact legal row.
Footer.avoidWhen: Do not use the full variant for a short footer that only needs legal text and a few links.
Footer.composition: Use FooterColumn for grouped navigation in the default variant; use meta for compact secondary links.
Footer.accessibility: Keep link labels distinct and group footer navigation with meaningful headings.

Notification/InlineNotification.intent: Show a concise message in the context of the current page or form.
Notification/InlineNotification.whenToUse: Use for a form submission result or an inline status message.
Notification/InlineNotification.avoidWhen: Use Banner for page-level notices and InlineNotification for contextual messages; do not use Toast for required actions or long-form content.
Notification/InlineNotification.composition: Render near the content or field the message describes.
Notification/InlineNotification.accessibility: Default uses a status region; error uses an alert region. Keep the message clear without relying on color alone.
Notification/InlineNotification.example: <InlineNotification message="Changes saved." />; <InlineNotification message="Could not save changes." type="error" />

Tooltip.intent: Show brief supplementary text for a control.
Tooltip.whenToUse: Use when a concise hint or keyboard shortcut helps explain an action.
Tooltip.avoidWhen: Use only for supplementary text, never essential information or interactive content.
Tooltip.composition: Wrap one focusable trigger; keep the tooltip text short and let placement flip when it does not fit.
Tooltip.accessibility: The trigger references the tooltip with aria-describedby. The tooltip itself never receives focus.
Tooltip.example: <Tooltip content="Copy link" shortcut="⌘C"><Button variant="tertiary" iconOnly iconLeft="copy" label="" /></Tooltip>
